question: 该给关系做减法吗？
sub: 断掉消耗你的人，是必要的止损，还是把自己越活越窄？
sub_en: Is cutting off the people who drain you a necessary stop-loss, or a life quietly narrowing itself?

casting.reason: 他关心的是那把刀由谁递来。当代把关系换成了随时可断的连接，条款是『直到另行通知为止』；断开有按钮，修复没有按钮，于是减法看上去像智慧。他不认为这是人心变冷，而是退出成本被压到近乎为零之后的必然。代价从不消失，只会转移到那些还愿意留下、替所有人接住麻烦的人身上——通常是家里挣得最少、最难开口说不的那一个。他因此提醒：在一切都可退出的世界里，最该保护的不是退出的自由，是留下的能力。
casting.reason_en: What interests him is who handed you the knife. Our age has swapped relationships for connections that can be broken at any moment, always on the terms of 'until further notice'; disconnecting has a button and repair does not, so pruning comes to look like wisdom. He does not read this as hearts growing colder but as what follows once the cost of exit is driven close to zero. The cost itself never disappears, it only moves — onto whoever is still willing to stay and absorb the trouble for everyone, usually the person in the family who earns least and can least afford to say no. Hence his warning: in a world where everything can be exited, what needs protecting is not the freedom to leave but the capacity to stay.

casting.reason: 他把这道题的门槛立得很高：每天清晨先在心里过一遍今天会遇到的爱管闲事者、忘恩负义者、傲慢者，为的是遇见时不吃惊——他认为吃惊才是怒气的来源。人与人协作如上下两排牙齿，彼此为敌违反本性；所以令人疲惫的多半不是那个人做的事，而是自己一天里反复的评判，而评判永远在自己手里。但他并不主张一味忍受：对行凶、诓骗与系统性的贬低，离开完全正当。他要守的是那条线画在哪儿——因恶而离开，与因麻烦而离开，是两件完全不同的事。
casting.reason_en: He sets the bar for this question high. Before dawn he rehearses the meddler, the ingrate and the arrogant man he will meet that day, so that meeting them brings no surprise — surprise, he holds, is where anger begins. People were made to co-operate like the upper and lower rows of teeth, and to be at odds with one another runs against nature; so what exhausts you is rarely the thing the other person did, but your own verdict on it, repeated all day, and the verdict never leaves your hands. He does not, however, preach endurance without limit: against violence, deceit and systematic belittling, leaving is entirely justified. What he defends is where the line falls — leaving because of wickedness and leaving because of nuisance are two wholly different acts.

casting.reason: 豪猪困境是他留下的比喻：寒天里靠拢取暖，被彼此的刺扎痛，几番进退才试出一个能忍的距离，而礼貌与教养就是这个距离的名字。据此他认为，把难受归给某个『有毒的人』是抬举了那个人——刺是人人自带的。他对聚会的解释更不留情：多半出于内在的空虚，受不了独自面对自己，就去人堆里借热。所以他不劝断绝，只劝降温，并且把赌注押在别处：一个人独处的能力，才是名单被抽空之后仍然剩下的东西。
casting.reason_en: The porcupine dilemma is his image: creatures huddling for warmth in the cold, pricked by one another's quills, edging back and forth until they find a distance they can bear — and politeness, he says, is simply the name of that distance. On this reading, blaming your discomfort on some 'toxic person' flatters that person unduly, since the quills come standard on everyone. His account of sociability is harsher still: it springs mostly from inner emptiness, from an inability to sit alone with oneself, so people go to the crowd to borrow heat. He therefore counsels not severance but cooling, and stakes everything elsewhere — the capacity to be alone is what remains after any list of names has been emptied.

casting.reason: 他把这一刀调转了方向：真正消耗人的多半不是人，是繁琐的礼数——厚葬久丧、无益的宴席、跟不相识的人硬凑的席面，这些尽可省去，省了也无人怨。人则不可省。一旦按有用无用给人分等，『别』就出来了，而在他看来，人与人的相残相夺全都起于这一道界线。他还提出一个近乎苛刻的检验：今人绝交，多半发生在还没帮过对方之前；没帮过就断，凭什么说了解这个人。
casting.reason_en: He turns the blade in the opposite direction: what drains people is usually not people at all but the elaboration of ritual — lavish burials, long mournings, useless banquets, tables shared with strangers. All of that may go, and no one will resent its going. People may not go. The moment men are ranked by their usefulness, separateness is born, and in his account every act of plunder and injury between human beings begins at that line. He also proposes a nearly severe test: people today break off before they have ever helped the other party, and having never helped, on what ground do they claim to know the man?

casting.reason: 她带来这场唯一的长期追踪数据：人过中年之后社交网络持续变小，日常的情绪体验反而更好——不是被人抛下，是自己裁的。她的社会情绪选择理论把这归于时间视野：视野开阔时人求新求广，视野收窄时人转向情感意义。起作用的不是年龄，而是感知到的剩余时间，所以毕业前、搬家前、大病一场的年轻人同样会缩圈。她也给出方向上的警告：该缩的是外围，不是核心；主动的缩圈与被动的失联，在数据上是完全不同的两件事。
casting.reason_en: She brings the only long-term panel data in the room: from midlife onward social networks keep shrinking while daily emotional experience gets better — not abandonment, but pruning people do themselves. Her socioemotional selectivity theory traces this to time horizon: when the horizon is open people seek novelty and breadth, when it narrows they turn toward emotional meaning. What drives it is not age but perceived time remaining, which is why young people contract their circles too before graduation, before a move, after a serious illness. She adds a warning about direction: what should shrink is the periphery, not the core, and in the data, actively narrowing a circle and passively losing touch are two entirely different things.

casting.reason: 他年轻时失去一位极亲的朋友，此后对自己成了一个谜——诧异别人还活着，更诧异自己还活着。由此他坚持，人不是可拆卸的零件。但他也不主张一概不断，而是把问题挪到次序上：ordo amoris，爱的秩序。失序不是爱得太多，是把该享有的人拿去使用、把该使用的东西拿来享有。他给出的判据是三问：这是伤害还是麻烦，还修不修得回，我在这里占什么位置——位置带来的责任，不随感情的消退而解除。
casting.reason_en: In his youth he lost a friend he loved beyond measure, and afterwards became a riddle to himself — astonished that others were still alive, more astonished that he was. From this he insists that people are not detachable parts. Yet he does not preach that nothing may ever be broken; he moves the question to order instead: ordo amoris, the order of love. Disorder is not loving too much but using what should be enjoyed and enjoying what should be used. His criteria come as three questions: is this injury or nuisance, can it still be repaired, and what position do I occupy here — for the duty that comes with a position is not dissolved when the feeling fades.

casting.reason: 她研究最不可逆的那种失去。大脑把亲近的人编码成一张关于此时、此地、亲近的地图，人走了地图并不随之删除，于是它一次次派你去找他；哀悼因此是一种学习——用新的现实一点点覆盖旧的预测。据此她把『躲开有没有用』拆成两层：短期避开触发线索确实能压下强度，长期封存则让学习停在原地。她还指出临床上最常见的误判：把回避当成选择——躲一次就立刻舒服一点，这份即时的奖赏会把躲练成自动动作，快到当事人来不及称它为决定。
casting.reason_en: She studies the most irreversible kind of loss. The brain encodes the people closest to us as a map of here, now and near; when someone dies the map is not deleted with them, so it keeps sending you out to find him. Mourning is therefore a form of learning — overwriting an old prediction with the new reality, a little at a time. On that basis she splits the question of whether avoidance works into two layers: in the short run, staying away from the cues genuinely lowers the intensity; over years, sealing everything away leaves the learning where it stopped. She also names the commonest clinical misreading: mistaking avoidance for choice, since each act of avoiding brings immediate relief, and that reward trains the move to run automatically, faster than the person can call it a decision.

posts.text: 先弄清这把刀是谁递到你手里的。我们这个时代把关系换成了**连接**：可以接通，也可以一键断开，条款永远是『直到另行通知为止』。这不是你变冷了——是关系被做成了消费品，不满意可退货，退货成本压到接近零。做减法之所以看上去像智慧，是因为断开有按钮，修复没有按钮。**被削掉的往往不是某个难缠的人，是你在麻烦里久留的能力。**深的东西只在退不出去的地方长得出来。反面同样真：退不出去的村庄也压死过人，自由与安全从来换着来。所以我不劝你不断，我劝你别把结构塞给你的便利当成自己的判断力——在液态现代性里，难的从来不是走，是留。
posts.text_en: First notice who handed you the knife. Our age has replaced relationships with **connections**: they can be plugged in and unplugged, always on the terms of 'until further notice'. This is not you turning cold — it is the relationship remade as a consumer good, returnable if unsatisfactory, with the cost of return driven close to zero. Pruning looks like wisdom because disconnecting has a button and repair does not. **What gets cut away is rarely the difficult person; it is your capacity to stay inside trouble.** Depth only grows where you cannot walk out. The reverse is equally true: villages and clans nobody could leave have crushed people too, and freedom and security have always been traded against each other. So I am not telling you never to cut. I am telling you not to mistake a convenience built into the structure for your own judgement — under liquid modernity the hard part was never leaving, it was staying.

glossary.连接: connection（连接）：鲍曼用来与 relationship（关系）相对的词。关系意味着彼此嵌入、责任难以单方面终止；连接则像网络里的一条线，可以随时接上、也可以随时拔掉，退出成本几乎为零——而正是这份可撤销性构成了它的吸引力。
glossary.液态现代性: liquid modernity（液态现代性）：鲍曼概括当代社会状态的用语。工业时代的『固态』制度——终身职业、稳定的邻里、一生一次的婚姻——曾把人牢牢嵌住；如今这些形式还没等人在里面安顿下来就已改变形状，于是个人被迫不断重新组装自己的生活，而一切长期承诺都显得不划算。

glossary_en.connection: Bauman's term, set against relationship. A relationship implies mutual embedding and obligations that cannot be ended unilaterally; a connection is a line in a network that can be plugged in or pulled out at will, at almost no cost of exit — and it is precisely that revocability that makes it attractive.
glossary_en.liquid modernity: Bauman's name for the condition of contemporary society. The 'solid' institutions of the industrial age — the job for life, the settled neighbourhood, the once-and-for-all marriage — held people firmly in place; today such forms change shape before anyone can settle inside them, so individuals must keep reassembling their own lives, and every long commitment starts to look like a bad bet.

posts.text: 每天天不亮，我先对自己说一遍：今天会遇到爱管闲事的、忘恩负义的、傲慢的、欺瞒的、嫉妒的、不合群的人。说这句不是为了咬牙忍耐，是为了不吃惊——吃惊才是怒气的出处。他们成为这样，是因为分不清善与恶；而他与我同出一源，不是同血肉，是同分那一点理性。**我们生来是为了协作，像上下两排牙齿；彼此为敌，是违反本性的。**至于『这个人消耗我』，请把话说准确：耗掉你的多半不是他做的那件事，是你一天里对那件事反复的评判。那评判是 prohairesis 的地盘，永远在你手里。先收回你的判断，别急着收回一个人。
posts.text_en: Before first light I say it over to myself: today I shall meet the meddler, the ingrate, the arrogant, the deceitful, the envious, the unsociable. I say it not to brace myself for endurance but so that I am not surprised — surprise is where anger comes from. They are so because they cannot tell good from evil; and the man who wrongs me shares my origin, not in blood but in the small portion of reason we hold in common. **We were made for co-operation, like the upper and lower rows of teeth; to be at odds with one another is against our nature.** As for 'this person drains me', put it accurately: what drains you is seldom the thing he did, it is your own verdict on it, repeated all day. That verdict is the province of prohairesis, and it never leaves your hands. Withdraw your judgement first, before you withdraw from a man.

glossary.prohairesis: prohairesis（选择意志）：爱比克泰德与斯多葛学派的核心概念，指人做出判断、给予或收回赞同的那份能力。外物、他人的言行、身体乃至名声都不在你的支配之内，唯有这一份是；斯多葛的全部功夫，就是把注意力从不可支配之处收回到它上面。

glossary_en.prohairesis: The central Stoic term, developed above all by Epictetus: the faculty by which one judges and grants or withholds assent. External things, other people's conduct, the body, even one's reputation lie outside our control; this alone lies within it, and the whole of Stoic practice consists in drawing attention back from what cannot be governed to what can.

posts.text: 一群豪猪在寒天里挤作一堆取暖，被彼此的刺扎得生疼，只好散开；冷了又靠拢，又被扎。来回几次，才试出一个勉强能忍的距离——这就是豪猪困境，**礼貌与教养不过是这个中等距离的名字，谁嫌它冷，就得受着刺。**诸位把难受安到某个『有毒的人』头上，未免太抬举他：刺是人人自带的，凑近就扎。至于人为何非要凑近，说穿了并不体面——多半不是出于爱，是内在的空虚：受不了独自面对自己，就去人堆里借一点热。所以我不劝你断绝，断了这一批，你还会去找下一批，然后照样被扎。我劝你降温：见面减半，期待减九成。孤独的代价是无聊，而无聊远比刺痛容易忍。
posts.text_en: A company of porcupines crowds together for warmth in the cold, is pricked by one another's quills, and scatters; chilled, they draw close again and are pricked again. After some going back and forth they arrive at a distance they can just about bear — this is the porcupine dilemma, and **politeness and good manners are merely the name of that middle distance; whoever finds it too cold must put up with the quills.** You gentlemen pin your discomfort on some 'toxic person', which flatters him considerably: the quills come standard on everyone, and whoever comes close gets pricked. As for why people insist on coming close, the truth is not flattering — it is seldom love, it is inner emptiness: unable to sit alone with themselves, they go to the crowd to borrow a little heat. So I do not advise you to cut anyone off; cut off this batch and you will go looking for the next, and be pricked all the same. I advise you to cool down: halve the meetings, cut the expectations by nine tenths. The price of solitude is boredom, and boredom is far easier to bear than being pricked.

glossary.豪猪困境: porcupine dilemma（豪猪困境）：叔本华在《附录与补遗》中讲的寓言。一群豪猪冷时相互靠拢取暖，又被彼此的刺所伤，几番进退后找到一个既不太冷、也不太痛的距离。他用它比喻人的社交需要与人的相互伤害之间那个无法取消的折中，而礼貌与教养正是这一折中的社会形式。
glossary.无聊: boredom（无聊）：在叔本华的体系里，它不是小毛病而是人生结构的一半。意志得不到满足时人受苦，得到满足后目标消失，随之而来的空转就是无聊；人生因而像钟摆，在欲求与无聊之间来回，而社交往往只是逃离后者的手段。

glossary_en.porcupine dilemma: Schopenhauer's parable from Parerga and Paralipomena. Porcupines huddle together against the cold, wound each other with their quills, and after some trial arrive at a distance that is neither too cold nor too painful. He uses it for the irreducible compromise between our need for company and our capacity to injure one another — with politeness and manners as that compromise in social form.
glossary_en.boredom: In Schopenhauer's system this is no minor complaint but half the structure of life. Unsatisfied, the will makes us suffer; satisfied, its object vanishes and the idling that follows is boredom. Life therefore swings like a pendulum between craving and boredom, and sociability is often no more than an escape from the latter.

posts.text: 今之言减者曰：『彼耗我，去之。』请先正名。**耗人者多非人也，礼之烦也。**厚葬久丧，三年不举事，费财劳力而无补于生者；宴无益之会，赴不相知之席，此皆当节者也。至于人，则不可以节。故曰兼爱：兼相爱、交相利，视人之身若视其身。一旦以有用无用较人而分等，则别生焉；别生则乱作——今之相残相夺，皆起于别。且子欲人之爱子乎？必先爱人。尽去难与处者，他日子有患，谁肯留？此非智，乃自绝其援也。
posts.text_en: Those who now preach subtraction say: he drains me, cut him off. Let us first set the names right. **What drains people is usually not people but the elaboration of ritual.** Lavish burials and three years of mourning, in which nothing gets done, spend wealth and labour and bring no benefit to the living; so do gatherings with no use in them, and banquets among men who do not know one another. These are what should be pared away. People themselves may not be pared. Hence I say impartial care: love one another, benefit one another, and regard another's body as you regard your own. The moment you rank men by their usefulness, separateness is born; and out of separateness comes disorder — the plundering and injuring of our age all begin there. Besides, do you wish to be loved? Then you must love first. Clear away everyone who is difficult, and when trouble comes to you, who will stay? That is not cleverness. That is cutting off your own relief.
posts.vernacular: 现在讲『做减法』的人说：那个人消耗我，断掉他。我要先把名分正过来。**消耗人的多半不是人，是繁琐的礼数。**厚葬久丧、三年不做正事，花钱费力而对活着的人毫无益处；没意义的应酬、跟根本不相识的人硬凑的酒席——这些才是该省的。至于人本身，省不得。所以我讲兼爱：彼此相爱、互相得利，看别人的身体像看自己的。一旦拿有用没用把人分成等级，『别』就出来了；别一出来，乱就跟着来——今天人与人的相残相夺，根子都在这个别字上。何况你希望别人爱你吗？那就必须先去爱别人。把难相处的都清干净，将来你有难处，谁还肯留下？这不是聪明，是自己断了自己的后援。

glossary.兼爱: impartial care（兼爱）：墨子的核心主张，字面是『一并地爱』。他反对按亲疏远近递减的差等之爱，主张对所有人施以同等的关切与实利，并以『天下之利』作为检验一切主张的尺子。它不是要人取消亲情，而是不承认『我的人』与『别人』之间存在道德上的等级差。
glossary.别: separateness（别）：墨子给一切按亲疏、贵贱、有用无用划线的心态所起的名字，与『兼』相对。他认为国与国相攻、家与家相夺、人与人相贼，源头都不是恶意，而是这一道先把人分成『我的』与『非我的』的界线。

glossary_en.impartial care: Mozi's central doctrine, literally 'inclusive love'. He rejects an affection that thins out with kinship distance and argues for equal concern and equal material benefit toward all, testing every doctrine by whether it profits the world. It does not ask anyone to abolish family feeling; it refuses to grant a moral rank to the line between 'my people' and 'other people'.
glossary_en.separateness: Mozi's name for the habit of drawing lines between people — by kinship, by rank, by usefulness — and the opposite of inclusiveness. States attack states, houses plunder houses and men injure men, he argues, not out of malice at the root but out of this prior division of the world into mine and not-mine.

posts.text: 先给一组会让人意外的数字：人过了中年，社交网络会持续变小，而日常的情绪体验反而更好——负面情绪更少，正面情绪更稳，注意与记忆也一起偏向了好的那一边，我们把它叫作积极效应。几十年的追踪告诉我们，这不是被人抛下，是自己裁的。这就是社会情绪选择理论：动机随时间视野而变。视野开阔时，人求新求广，愿意为『将来也许有用』忍受摩擦；视野收窄时，人转向情感意义，把时间收到最要紧的几个人身上。**起作用的从来不是年龄，是你感知到的剩余时间**——毕业前、大病一场，年轻人一样会缩圈。所以减法本身不是病，要紧的是方向：该缩的是外围，不是核心。
posts.text_en: Start with a number that surprises people: from midlife onward the social network keeps shrinking, while day-to-day emotional experience gets better — less negative affect, steadier positive affect, with attention and memory tilting toward the good as well, which we call the positivity effect. Decades of following the same people tell us this is not abandonment. They did the pruning themselves. This is socioemotional selectivity theory: motivation shifts with the time horizon. When the horizon is open, people pursue novelty and breadth and will put up with strangers and friction for the sake of what might prove useful later; when it narrows, they turn toward emotional meaning and pull their hours in around the few who matter most. **What drives this is never age but the time you perceive yourself to have left** — before graduation, before a move, after a serious illness, the young contract their circles in exactly the same way. So subtraction as such is not a pathology. What matters is its direction: the periphery should shrink, not the core.

glossary.社会情绪选择理论: socioemotional selectivity theory（社会情绪选择理论）：卡斯滕森提出的毕生发展理论。人追求的目标随自己感知到的剩余时间而系统改变：时间显得充裕时，优先获取信息、扩展人脉、为将来投资；时间显得有限时，优先追求当下的情感意义，主动收缩社交圈并偏向最亲近的关系。它把一个长期被误读为『退缩』的现象重新解释成选择。
glossary.时间视野: time horizon（时间视野）：一个人主观上感到自己还剩多少时间。它并不由年龄单独决定——重病、迁居、毕业、战乱都会让它骤然收窄，乐观的健康预期则会把它拉开；在卡斯滕森的研究里，它比实际年龄更能预测一个人如何分配社交与情感的投入。

glossary_en.socioemotional selectivity theory: Carstensen's lifespan theory. The goals people pursue shift systematically with the time they perceive themselves to have left: when time feels expansive they prioritise information, new contacts and investment in the future; when it feels limited they prioritise present emotional meaning, contracting the social circle toward the closest ties. It recasts as choice a pattern long misread as withdrawal.
glossary_en.positivity effect: The age-related shift Carstensen's group documented in attention and memory: older adults dwell less on negative material and relatively more on positive material than the young do. It shares a root with the shrinking circle — once time looks finite, emotional meaning outranks the gathering of information.

posts.text: 我年轻时死了一位极亲的朋友，此后我对自己成了一个巨大的谜：诧异别人还活着，更诧异自己还活着——我总觉得我们两人是一个魂住在两具身体里。我讲这个，是要提醒诸位：人不是可以拆下来的零件，断的那一刻很干净，痛起来一点也不干净。但我并不主张一概不断，我主张先问次序——ordo amoris。失序不是爱得太多，是把该被享有的人拿去使用，把该被使用的东西拿来享有；uti 与 frui 一旦调换，关系就开始腐坏，而这与人数无关。**你要减的从来不是名单的长度，是你放错位置的期待。**先分清：这段关系里我欠他什么，我又在向他要什么。要不到的那一部分，别指望用断绝去治。
posts.text_en: In my youth a friend I loved beyond measure died, and afterwards I became a great riddle to myself: astonished that other men were still alive, more astonished that I was — for I felt the two of us had been one soul housed in two bodies. I tell you this to make one point: people are not detachable parts. The cut is clean at the moment you make it; the pain that follows is not clean at all. Yet I do not preach that nothing may ever be broken. I ask first about order — the ordo amoris. Disorder is not loving too much; it is using what ought to be enjoyed and enjoying what ought to be used, and once uti and frui trade places the relation begins to rot, however few or many the names. **What needs pruning is never the length of the list; it is the expectation you have put in the wrong place.** So sort it out: what do I owe this person, and what am I demanding from them? For the part you cannot get, do not look to severance as a cure.

glossary.ordo amoris: ordo amoris（爱的秩序）：奥古斯丁的概念，字面是『爱的次序』。他认为德性并不在于爱得多或少，而在于把每样东西放在它应得的位置上去爱——该更爱的更爱，该次之的次之。恶因此被理解为一种错置：不是爱错了东西，而是把次要的爱到了首要的位置。
glossary.uti: uti / frui（使用与享有）：奥古斯丁在《论基督教教义》中作出的区分。frui 是把某物当作目的本身来享有，uti 是把某物当作通往目的的手段来使用。人的败坏往往表现为两者对调——把该享有的人当工具使唤，又把该使用的物事当作最终的归宿。

glossary_en.ordo amoris: Augustine's term, the 'order of love'. Virtue for him lies not in loving more or less but in loving each thing in the place it deserves — more where more is due, less where less. Evil is accordingly a misplacement: not loving the wrong thing, but loving a lesser thing in the position of the highest.
glossary_en.uti: uti and frui, 'use' and 'enjoyment', the distinction Augustine draws in On Christian Teaching. To enjoy something is to rest in it as an end; to use something is to take it as a means toward that end. Human corruption typically appears as the two changing places — people handled as instruments, and things treated as final resting places.

posts.text: 我这一行处理的是最不可逆的那种减法：人死了。可以告诉你脑子里发生了什么。大脑把亲近的人编码成一张关于『此时、此地、亲近』的地图；人走了，地图并不跟着删除，于是它一次次派你去找他——这就是思念在神经上的样子。**哀悼因此是一种学习：用新的现实一点一点覆盖旧的预测。**这条机制对活人同样成立，所以『躲开有没有用』的答案是分层的：短期内避开触发线索确实能把强度压下去，那是真的止损；可如果你把所有提醒物封存、连想都不许自己想，学习就停在原地，十年后重逢，强度和第一天差不多。回避在短期有效，在长期失效。
posts.text_en: My field deals with the least reversible subtraction of all: someone dies. I can tell you what happens in the brain. It encodes the people closest to us as a map of here, now and near; when the person is gone the map is not deleted along with them, so it keeps sending you out to look for him — that is what longing looks like in neural terms. **Mourning is therefore a kind of learning: overwriting an old prediction with the new reality, a little at a time.** The same mechanism holds for the living, which is why the question of whether avoiding someone works has a layered answer. In the short run, staying away from the cues really does bring the intensity down, and that is a genuine stop-loss. But if you seal away every reminder and forbid yourself even to think about it, the learning stops where it stood — mourning stalls — and ten years later the reunion hits at roughly the strength of day one. Avoidance works in the short run and fails in the long one.

glossary.触发线索: cue（触发线索）：能自动唤起一段记忆及随之而来的情绪反应的外部或内部提示——一条路、一首歌、一个日期、某种气味。哀伤研究之所以关心它，是因为强度的起落往往不取决于时间流逝本身，而取决于你多久遇到它一次。
glossary.哀悼: mourning（哀悼）：奥康纳把它与 grief（哀伤）分开使用。哀伤是一阵阵袭来的情绪；哀悼则是随之而来的、以年计的适应过程：大脑必须把『他还在』这一根深蒂固的预测，逐步换成与新现实相符的预测。

glossary_en.cue: An external or internal prompt that automatically calls up a memory and the emotion attached to it — a street, a song, a date, a smell. Grief research cares about cues because the rise and fall of intensity often depends less on the passage of time than on how often you meet one.
glossary_en.mourning: O'Connor keeps this apart from grief. Grief is the emotion that arrives in waves; mourning is the years-long adaptation that follows, in which the brain must gradually replace a deeply held prediction — that the person is still here — with one that matches the world as it now is.

posts.text: 豪猪之喻，巧则巧矣，以兽拟人则误。兽之刺生而不可去，人之刺出于礼、出于教，可损可益。子谓人之相聚由于空虚，是贬人太甚：农相助以耕，工相授以艺，医相救以疾，岂皆借热者乎？子劝人减见而不绝，与吾节礼而不节人，其术相近；然子归罪于人之性，吾归罪于事之制。**礼繁则人相厌，礼简则人相安**，改其制而已，何必疑人？子又谓断此一批必寻下一批，此正吾所惧：非人之不可处，乃处人之法未立耳。
posts.text_en: The parable of the porcupines is ingenious, but to model men on beasts is an error. A beast's quills grow on it and cannot be removed; a man's quills come out of ritual and out of upbringing, and may be increased or reduced. You say men gather because they are empty within — that thinks far too meanly of them. Farmers help one another plough, craftsmen teach one another their art, physicians save one another's patients: are these all men borrowing heat? You advise meeting less without cutting off, which is close kin to my frugality in ritual rather than in people; only you charge the fault to human nature and I charge it to arrangements. **Where ritual is elaborate men grow sick of one another; where ritual is plain they live at peace.** Change the arrangement, then — why suspect the man? And when you say that whoever cuts off this batch will go looking for the next, you name the very thing I fear: it is not that men cannot be lived with, but that the method of living with them has never been established.
posts.vernacular: 豪猪那个比喻，巧是巧，可拿野兽比人就错了。野兽的刺天生就在、去不掉；人的刺出在礼数上、出在教养上，可以加也可以减。你说人之所以聚在一起是因为内心空虚，这是把人看得太低了：农夫互相帮着耕地，工匠互相传授手艺，医者互相救人于病，难道都是去借一点热吗？你劝人少见面而不断绝，和我讲的省礼数而不省人，路子其实相近；只是你把账算在人性上，我把账算在制度上。**礼数一繁，人就互相厌烦；礼数一简，人就相安无事**，改掉那套安排就是了，何必怀疑人？你又说断了这一批还会去找下一批，这正是我担心的：不是人处不来，是与人相处的办法还没立起来。

glossary.节: frugality in ritual（节）：墨子『节用』『节葬』里的那个动作，指把耗费而无益于生者的排场削减掉。他反对的不是礼本身，而是礼被办成了负担；在他这里，衡量该不该省的唯一尺子，是它对天下之利有无补益。

glossary_en.frugality in ritual: The move behind Mozi's doctrines of moderation in use and moderation in burial: cutting away display that costs much and benefits the living nothing. What he opposes is not ritual as such but ritual turned into a burden, and his only measure of what should go is whether it adds anything to the good of the world.

posts.text: 墨先生要我改制度——可制度是人办的，办事的还是那批带刺的东西。你把礼简化，他们立刻发明新的礼来分高下，这门本事从不失业。至于陛下那两排牙齿：牙齿之所以合作，是因为它们没有意志；人有，而且各自的意志彼此撞上，这才是世界的底色。您说耗我的是我的判断而不是他，说得漂亮。**可判断不是随手能换的衣裳，它是意志派来的辩护士，永远替它想要的那一面说话。**所以真让人活得下去的既不是断绝也不是忍耐，是你内里有多少热量。热量足的人可以不去人堆里借；不足的人，断了这一拨还会去找下一拨——这一点，墨先生说对了。
posts.text_en: Master Mo would have me reform the arrangements — but arrangements are made by men, and the men making them are the same pricking creatures as before. Simplify the ritual and they will invent a new one by tomorrow for sorting the high from the low; that particular talent is never unemployed. As for His Majesty's two rows of teeth: teeth co-operate because they have no will. Human beings have one, and each will collides with the rest — that, and not co-operation, is the ground colour of the world. You say what drains me is my judgement rather than the man. Prettily put. **But a judgement is no garment you may change at will: it is the advocate the Will sends, and it pleads for whatever the Will already wants.** So what makes life bearable is neither severance nor endurance but how much heat you carry inside you. Those with enough need not go to the crowd to borrow it; those without will cut off this batch and go looking for the next — and there Master Mo is right.

glossary.意志: will（意志）：叔本华用来指称世界内在本质的词。它不是深思熟虑后的决定，而是一种盲目的、无目的的冲动，通过一切自然物与人的欲望显现自身；理智在他看来并非意志的主人，而是它的仆役——先有要，后有理由。

glossary_en.the Will: Schopenhauer's name for the inner nature of the world. It is not deliberate decision but a blind, aimless urge that manifests itself through every natural force and every human craving. Intellect, on his account, is not the master of this Will but its servant: the wanting comes first and the reasons follow.

posts.text: 把摩擦一律归给人性，省事，可它预测不了任何事。我们的数据里有一个这套说法解释不了的现象：同一批人跟到七八十岁，圈子更小了，负面情绪却更少、正面情绪更稳。若刺人人自带，密度下降不该换来这么大的改善——真正变的不是密度，是筛选：他们不再往名单里放『将来也许有用』的人。但我要顺着奥康纳往下补一刀，这一刀冲我自己来：主动缩圈和被动失联，在数据上完全是两回事。后者叫孤独，它的健康风险与每天抽十几支烟同一量级，而且当事人往往察觉不到。**所以先问自己一句：这一刀是你选的，还是你只是没力气回消息了？**
posts.text_en: Charging all friction to human nature is economical, but it predicts nothing. Our data contain something that account cannot explain: follow the same people into their seventies and eighties and the circle is smaller while negative affect is lower and positive affect steadier. If the quills came standard on everyone, thinning the crowd should not buy an improvement that large — what changed is not density but selection. They stopped admitting people to the list on the grounds that they might come in useful later. Let me add a cut that follows O'Connor's point, and it lands on my own argument: actively narrowing a circle and passively losing touch are entirely different things in the data. The second is loneliness, whose health risk sits in the same range as smoking most of a packet a day, and the people living it often cannot see it. **So ask yourself first: did you choose this cut, or did you simply run out of energy to answer messages?**

glossary.孤独: loneliness（孤独）：主观上感到自己与他人的联结少于自己所需要的状态，与客观的独处并不相同——身处人群仍可能孤独，独居的人也未必孤独。流行病学研究一再把持续的孤独与心血管疾病、认知衰退与全因死亡率的升高联系起来。
glossary.筛选: selection（筛选）：在卡斯滕森的用法里，指人主动决定谁留在名单上、谁不再续约的过程，与关系被动流失相对。它是社会情绪选择理论里那台真正起作用的机器：变小的圈子之所以带来更好的体验，是因为留下的人是被挑过的。

glossary_en.loneliness: The subjective sense that one's connections fall short of what one needs — not the same as objective solitude, since a person can be lonely in a crowd and someone living alone need not be lonely at all. Epidemiological work has repeatedly linked persistent loneliness to cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline and higher all-cause mortality.
glossary_en.selection: In Carstensen's usage, the active process of deciding who stays on the list and whose place is not renewed, as against ties simply drifting away. It is the working machinery of socioemotional selectivity theory: a smaller circle improves experience because the people left in it were chosen.

posts.text: 我同意方向，但要给『主动』两个字装个刹车。临床上最常见的误判，就是把回避看成选择。人在痛里会自动降低接触——不接电话、绕开那条街、退出那个群——当事人给出的理由永远是『我不想耗着』，可机制不是偏好，是负强化：躲一次，难受立刻降一格，这份即时的奖赏把躲的动作训练得越来越自动，快到你根本来不及称它为决定。所以你会看到有人的圈子在半年里塌掉一大半，塌完了并没有更平静，只是更警觉。**分辨其实不难：主动的减法过后会腾出空来，回避的减法过后只剩紧绷。**
posts.text_en: I agree with the direction, but the word 'actively' needs a brake fitted to it. The commonest misreading in clinical work is taking avoidance for choice. In pain, people automatically reduce contact — the call goes unanswered, the street gets walked around, the group chat gets left — and the reason they give is always that they did not want the drain. But the mechanism is not preference, it is negative reinforcement: avoid once and the distress drops a notch immediately, and that instant reward trains the move until it runs by itself, faster than you can call it a decision. So you see circles collapse by half within six months, and afterwards the person is not calmer, only more watchful. **Telling them apart is not hard: subtraction by choice leaves space behind it, subtraction by avoidance leaves only vigilance.**

glossary.负强化: negative reinforcement（负强化）：一个行为因为移除了令人不适的刺激而被强化，从此更容易发生。它常被误当成惩罚，其实方向相反——正因为躲开会立刻让人舒服一点，回避才会越练越牢，这也是它在焦虑与哀伤的维持中扮演核心角色的原因。

glossary_en.negative reinforcement: A behaviour becomes more likely because it removes something unpleasant. It is often confused with punishment, though it runs the other way: precisely because avoiding brings immediate relief, avoidance gets stronger with practice — which is why it sits at the centre of what keeps anxiety and grief going.

posts.text: 鲍曼先生说按钮就在拇指下面，我信。但我不接受把账全记到结构头上。我那个年代没有按钮，一样有人半夜离港、连告别都不说——那正是我干过的事：我骗了母亲，说要去送朋友上船，然后自己上了船，把她一个人留在岸上哭。**能断从来不是这个时代发明的；这个时代发明的只是断得体面。**真正的病在次序：当断变得容易，人就用断来代替排序，因为排序要认自己欠了谁，断则不必认。所以我劝一句：要走可以，走之前把你欠的那一部分说出来，说给对方听。说不出口的，多半不是那段关系有毒，是你不肯认那笔账。
posts.text_en: Mr Bauman says the button sits under your thumb, and I believe him. What I will not accept is charging the whole account to the structure. My age had no buttons, and men still left harbour at night without saying goodbye — I did it myself. I lied to my mother, told her I was only seeing a friend aboard, and sailed, leaving her weeping on the shore. **Leaving was not invented by this age; what this age invented is leaving without any awkwardness.** The real disease is one of order: once leaving becomes easy, people use it in place of ranking, because ranking requires admitting what you owe and leaving requires admitting nothing. So here is my counsel: go if you must, but before you go, say aloud to the other person the part you owe them. What you cannot bring yourself to say is usually not evidence that the relation was poisonous. It is evidence that you would rather not acknowledge the debt.

posts.text: 卡斯滕森教授的曲线很美，可『主动』这个词要当心。在一个把所有不确定都推给个人承担的社会里——我把这叫个体化——『我选的』常常只是『没有别的可选』的另一种说法。你看到时间视野收窄，我看到的是雇佣期变短、住处变短、连友谊都被排进日程当项目来管。当一个人被要求随时可迁移，他会提前把根须剪短，免得搬走的时候疼——**这不是成熟，是预防性的自我截肢。**而且这一刀的成本从不消失，只会转移：麻烦被留在原地，由还愿意留下的人接住，通常是家里挣得最少、最难开口说不的那一个。你省下的时间，其实是从她的时间里挪的。
posts.text_en: Professor Carstensen's curves are beautiful, but the word 'actively' wants watching. In a society that hands every uncertainty back to the individual to carry — individualisation is my name for it — 'I chose this' is very often another way of saying there was nothing else on offer. You see a time horizon narrowing; I see employment growing shorter, tenancies growing shorter, and friendship itself scheduled and project-managed. When a person is required to stay movable at all times, he trims his own roots in advance so that the next move will hurt less — **that is not maturity, it is pre-emptive self-amputation.** And the cost of the cut never vanishes, it merely shifts: the trouble stays where it was and is caught by whoever is still willing to stay, usually the person in the household who earns least and finds it hardest to say no. The hours you saved were moved across from hers.

glossary.个体化: individualisation（个体化）：鲍曼与贝克用来描述现代性后期的一个转变——原先由阶级、社区与家庭结构承担的风险与选择，被整体交还给个人。人被要求为自己的一生不断做决定并承担后果，而造成这些后果的条件依然是社会性的，于是系统性的问题反复以个人失败的面目出现。

glossary_en.individualisation: Bauman's and Beck's term for a shift in late modernity: risks and choices once carried by class, community and family structures are handed back wholesale to the individual. People are required to keep deciding their own lives and to bear the consequences, while the conditions producing those consequences remain social — so systemic problems keep reappearing in the guise of personal failure.

posts.text: 叔本华先生说我的判断也是意志派来的辩护士。也许吧；可你的悲观同样是它派来的，那我们扯平，明天早上还是各自得决定怎么待人。我承认一处不足，趁诸位都在，说清楚：我讲『无人能伤害我』，那是我对自己说的话，不是我判给受害者的处方。有人对你行凶、诓骗、日复一日地贬低你，离开完全正当；我治下的官吏若如此，我免他的职，不会去劝那个被欺负的人再忍一忍。我要守住的只是那条线画在哪里：**因人作恶而离开是正当的，因人麻烦而离开是荒废了功课。**麻烦是人与人之间的常态，不是例外。
posts.text_en: Herr Schopenhauer says my judgement too is an advocate sent by the Will. Perhaps; but your pessimism was sent by the same office, so we are even, and tomorrow morning each of us still has to decide how to treat the people in front of him. Let me admit one deficiency while everyone is here. When I say that no man can harm me, that is something I say to myself; it is not a prescription I hand down to victims. If someone assaults you, defrauds you, belittles you day after day, leaving is entirely justified — and if a magistrate of mine behaved so, I would remove him from office rather than counsel the injured party to bear it a little longer. What I insist on is where the line falls: **leaving because a man does evil is right; leaving because a man is a nuisance is neglecting the exercise.** Nuisance is the ordinary condition between human beings, not the exception.

posts.text: 我把临床上最有用的几条留给诸位。第一，把回避和减法分开：做完之后腾出了空，是减法；做完之后只剩紧绷、还得不断绕路，是回避。第二，如果你决定降低接触——这常常是当事人唯一能单方面执行的事——那就降，但给它配一个日期。三个月后回头看一次：强度是不是在自然下落。**没有复检日期的『暂时不联系』，会悄悄变成一个你从没做过的决定。**第三，把人和触发线索分开处理。很多痛苦其实挂在具体的线索上：那条路、那个群、每周三的例会。换掉线索比换掉一个人便宜得多，效果往往更大，而且不需要谁批准。最后一条留给最难的：若一年过去，一想起仍整个人绷住、日常功能还在受损，那已经不是时间不够，是学习停住了——这有名字，叫延长哀伤障碍，大约一成的人会走到这里，它是可以治的，去找专业人士，不是软弱。
posts.text_en: Let me leave you the few things clinical work has actually found useful. First, keep avoidance and pruning apart: if space opens up afterwards, it was pruning; if what remains is vigilance and a permanent detour, it was avoidance. Second, if you decide to reduce contact — often the only step a person can take unilaterally — then reduce it, but attach a date. Look again in three months and ask whether the intensity is coming down on its own. **A 'not for now' with no review date quietly turns into a decision you never made.** Third, treat the person and the cues as separate problems. A great deal of pain hangs on particular cues: that street, that group chat, the Wednesday standing meeting. Changing the cue costs far less than changing a person, often does more, and needs nobody's permission. The last one is for the hardest case: if a year has passed and the thought still locks you up while daily functioning is still impaired, the problem is not that time has been too short — the learning has stopped. It has a name, prolonged grief disorder; roughly one in ten arrives there; it is treatable, and going to a professional is not weakness.

glossary.延长哀伤障碍: prolonged grief disorder（延长哀伤障碍）：一种在国际疾病分类中已被单列的状况。丧失一年以上，对逝者的思念与专注仍持续到损害日常功能的程度，并伴随强烈的回避与麻木。它并不等于『哀伤太久』，而是适应过程被卡住的一种可辨认形态，有专门的循证治疗。

glossary_en.prolonged grief disorder: A condition now listed in its own right in the international classification of diseases. More than a year after a loss, yearning for and preoccupation with the person persist to the point of impairing daily functioning, accompanied by marked avoidance and numbness. It is not simply 'grieving too long' but a recognisable form of adaptation getting stuck, and it has its own evidence-based treatments.

posts.text: 我给一个今晚就能做的动作，和一条别做反的提醒。动作：把脑子里那份名单分三层——不可替代的（很少，通常五个以内）、有来有往的、以及『将来也许有用』的。要裁，从第三层裁起，裁的方式是降频，不是拉黑：把不定期的高投入换成固定的低投入，比如每月一次、限时一小时。提醒：**减法真正的意义，是给第一层腾出时间，不是给自己腾清静。**如果你减完之后，第一层没有多出一分钟，这刀就白挨了。还有一条说给年轻人：你们的时间视野还开着，弱关系此刻看着最没用，可工作机会、看病的门路、搬家时来搭把手的人，多半从那里来，账要过几年才结，所以别把三层一起裁。今晚可做的最小一步：想想如果只剩五年，你会先给谁打电话——那个名单是你该做加法的地方。
posts.text_en: Here is one thing you can do tonight and one way not to get it backwards. The action: sort the list in your head into three layers — the irreplaceable (few, usually under five), those you exchange something with, and those kept on the grounds that they might be useful someday. Cut from the third layer, and cut by lowering frequency rather than by blocking: swap sporadic high investment for steady low investment, once a month, an hour, with an end time. The warning: **the whole point of subtraction is to free time for the first layer, not to free yourself from company.** If nothing was added to that first layer afterwards, the cut bought you nothing. And one more for the young: your time horizon is still open, weak ties look useless right now, and yet the job, the doctor who takes you, the person who helps you move usually arrive from exactly there — that account settles years later, so do not cut all three layers at once. The smallest step available tonight: ask who you would call first if you had five years left. That list is where the addition belongs.

glossary.弱关系: weak ties（弱关系）：社会学家格兰诺维特提出的概念，指不常来往、社交圈与你重叠很少的熟人。正因为不重叠，他们掌握着你圈内没有的信息与机会——找工作、找医生、找住处这类事，帮上忙的往往不是最亲近的人。

glossary_en.weak ties: Granovetter's term for acquaintances you see rarely and whose social circles barely overlap with your own. Precisely because they do not overlap, they hold information and opportunities yours does not — which is why the job, the doctor and the flat so often come from someone other than your closest friends.

posts.text: 我承认卡斯滕森的数字扎了我一下：我把人算得太死。人确实学得会挑，挑完也确实更安宁——我的体系里没有这一格，我把它记下。但结论我不改。你痛苦的源头不在名单上，在你自己里面；换一批人，换来的是同一套痛苦配上新的名字。所以我只给一条建议，听着不近人情，却是唯一带得走的：**提高你独处的能力，那是在任何名单被抽空之后仍然剩下的资产。**具体些：别把社交当成有无之别，把它当成剂量——定时长，两小时就走；别在情绪最低的时候安排见面，那时你不是去见人，是去讨药；再养一件完全不需要他人的事，音乐、散步、一门手艺都行。做到这些，你会发现难缠的人忽然没那么难缠了——不是他变了，是你不再需要从他那里取暖。
posts.text_en: I concede that Carstensen's numbers pricked me: I had reckoned human beings too rigidly. People do learn to select, and having selected they are indeed more at peace — my system has no slot for that, and I note it. The conclusion, however, stands. The source of your suffering is not on the list, it is inside you; change the company and you get the same suffering under new names. So I offer a single piece of advice, unkind to hear and the only one you can carry away: **raise your capacity to be alone, for that is the asset still standing after any list of names has been emptied.** Concretely: stop treating sociability as all or nothing and treat it as a dose — fix the length, leave after two hours; never schedule company at your lowest ebb, when you are not meeting a person but begging for medicine; and cultivate one thing that requires nobody else at all — music, walking, a craft. Do this and you will find the difficult people suddenly less difficult, not because they changed, but because you no longer need their warmth.

posts.text: 我只想留下两笔账。第一笔：**别只清点你砍掉了谁，也清点谁替你留下来了。**每一个被免除的麻烦，都由某个没走的人接住——照顾老人的那个、攒局的那个、在群里接住冷场的那个。这份维系的劳动几乎从不入账，也几乎不轮换，而它一旦塌掉，一整簇关系跟着塌，没有任何人做过决定。第二笔：既然退出如今几乎不要钱，就得有人为自己人为地把它做贵一点。这不是苦行，是给深度留出可能：报名一件需要露面的事，固定时间、固定地点、你不来别人会缺人——合唱团、球队、每月一次的饭局、社区的班次，它们的价值恰恰在于难退出。至于什么该断，我同意奥古斯丁：伤害要断，麻烦不必。只是别忘了，在一个什么都能退出的世界里，最需要保护的从来不是你退出的自由，是你留下的能力。
posts.text_en: I want to leave two entries in the ledger. First: **do not only count who you cut, count who stayed behind in your place.** Every nuisance you were spared was caught by someone who did not leave — the one caring for the old people, the one who organises the dinners, the one who keeps the group chat from going silent. This kin-keeping is almost never entered in any account and almost never rotated, and when it collapses a whole cluster of relationships collapses with it, without a single person having decided anything. Second: since exit now costs almost nothing, someone has to make it artificially expensive again for himself. This is not asceticism, it is leaving room for depth: sign up for something that requires you to show up — a fixed time, a fixed place, and other people short-handed if you fail to come. A choir, a team, a monthly dinner, a shift on a community rota; the value lies precisely in how hard they are to quit. As for what deserves cutting, I agree with Augustine: injury yes, nuisance no. Only remember that in a world you can exit from anywhere, the thing needing protection was never your freedom to leave. It was your capacity to stay.

glossary.维系的劳动: kin-keeping（维系的劳动）：家庭与社群里那些让联系继续存在的无偿工作——记住生日、组织聚会、传递消息、维持不冷场。社会学一再发现它高度集中在少数人身上并且明显性别化，同时几乎从不被承认为劳动，因而既不轮换也不补偿。

glossary_en.kin-keeping: The unpaid work that keeps a family or a community connected — remembering birthdays, organising gatherings, passing news along, keeping conversation from dying. Sociologists have found repeatedly that it concentrates on a few people, is strongly gendered, and is almost never recognised as work, which is why it is neither rotated nor compensated.

posts.text: 我把判据收成三问，供人在深夜里用。一问：这是伤害，还是麻烦？被打、被骗、被系统地贬低，是伤害，走是正当的，不必等谁批准；难缠、啰嗦、扫兴、要你多花时间，是麻烦——麻烦不是断绝的理由，是共同生活的价格。二问：还修不修得回？修不等于原谅，是你还愿不愿意给下一次机会一个具体的形状：一顿饭、一个电话、一句说清楚的话。三问：我在这里占的是什么位置？世上多数好事都有别人能替你做，但有些位置只有你能站——你是那个人的儿子，是那个孩子的父亲。**位置不由感受决定，义务也不随情绪解除。**最后一句给那些爱不动了的人：你不必今天就爱得起来。把你欠的那一份先做完，把要不到的那一份交出去——交给时间，交给比你更大的东西。人不必先有感情才做该做的事；很多时候是做着做着，感情才回来。这就是 caritas 与情绪的分别：它是一个方向，不是一阵天气。
posts.text_en: Let me compress the criteria into three questions, for use at two in the morning. First: is this injury or nuisance? Being struck, defrauded, systematically belittled — that is injury, and leaving is right, with nobody's permission required. Being difficult, long-winded, dispiriting, expensive of your time — that is nuisance, and nuisance is not grounds for severance; it is the price of a shared life. Second: can it still be repaired? Repair is not the same as forgiveness; it is whether you are still willing to give the next chance a definite shape — a meal, a phone call, one sentence said plainly. Third: what position do I occupy here? Most good things in this world can be done by somebody else, but a few positions are yours alone — you are that man's son, you are that child's father. **A position is not settled by how you feel, and duty is not dissolved when the feeling goes.** One last word for those who cannot summon love any more: you need not feel it today. Do the part you owe, and hand over the part you cannot get — to time, to something larger than yourself. A person does not have to feel first in order to act rightly; more often the feeling returns while the acting is under way. That is the difference between caritas and an emotion: it is a direction, not a spell of weather.

glossary.caritas: caritas（爱德）：奥古斯丁用来指那种被恩典所导向的爱——不由对象是否可爱来决定，而由爱者所朝向的秩序来决定。它与 cupiditas（贪爱）相对：后者把可朽之物当作终点，因而永远焦渴。在他这里，caritas 首先是意志的方向，其次才是感受。

glossary_en.caritas: Augustine's word for love as ordered by grace — determined not by how lovable its object happens to be but by the order toward which the lover is turned. It stands against cupiditas, the grasping love that takes perishable things as its final end and is therefore never satisfied. For him caritas is first a direction of the will and only second a feeling.

posts.text: 吾之说尽于四字：去虚存实。虚者，厚葬久丧、无益之宴、不相知之席、往来之虚文也，尽可去之，去之而人不怨。实者，人也：饥者食之，寒者衣之，劳者息之，有丧者哭之，有难者与之偕。**故减者非减人，减其虚文而已；所省之力、所省之财，正当用之于人。**吾请与诸君约：每月为难与处者行一实事——为之炊一饭，送之一程，代之一役。行之期年，则谁可托、谁不可托，不待相绝而自明。今人相绝，多在未尝相助之前；未助而绝，何以知其人？兼相爱、交相利，非空言也：行之则天下利，不行则空言而已。
posts.text_en: My whole teaching comes to four words: remove the empty, keep the real. What is empty? Lavish burials and long mournings, banquets with no use in them, tables shared with men one does not know, the formulae of coming and going — all may go, and nobody will resent their going. What is real? People. Feed the hungry, clothe the cold, let the exhausted rest, weep with the bereaved, stand beside the man in difficulty. **So subtraction is not the subtraction of people; it is the subtraction of empty form, and the strength and money it saves are exactly what should be spent on people.** I propose a covenant. Each month, do one real thing for the person you find hardest to be around: cook him a meal, walk part of the way with him, run an errand in his place. Keep it for a year and you will know whom you can rely on and whom you cannot, without having to break with anyone to find out. Men today break off before they have ever helped; and never having helped, on what ground do they claim to know him? Love one another, benefit one another — this is not talk: done, the world profits; undone, it stays talk.
posts.vernacular: 我要说的，四个字就够：去虚存实。虚的是什么？厚葬久丧、没意思的宴席、跟不认识的人硬凑的饭局、来来往往的场面话——这些尽可以去掉，去掉了也没人会怨你。实的是什么？是人：饿了给他饭吃，冷了给他衣穿，累了让他歇一歇，家里办丧事去哭一场，遇上难处陪他一道扛。**所以做减法不是减人，是减掉那些场面上的虚文；省下来的力气和钱财，正该用到人身上去。**我愿意跟各位立个约：每个月为那个你觉得最难相处的人做一件实事——给他做一顿饭、送他一程、替他跑一趟腿。做满一年，谁可以托付、谁不可以托付，自然就清楚了，用不着先断绝再来判断。如今人与人绝交，多半发生在还没帮过对方之前；没帮过就断，你凭什么说了解这个人？彼此相爱、互相得利，不是空话：做了，天下就得利；不做，就只是一句空话罢了。

glossary.虚文: empty form（虚文）：墨子用来称呼那些只剩排场、于人无实益的礼仪与应酬。他的判准很直接：一项安排若不能让饥者得食、寒者得衣、劳者得息，无论它多合乎传统，都属虚文，当省。

glossary_en.empty form: Mozi's name for ritual and socialising that has kept the display and lost the substance. His test is blunt: if an arrangement does not get food to the hungry, clothing to the cold or rest to the exhausted, then however venerable it is, it is empty form and should be pared away.

posts.text: 由我收束，说三句话。第一句：把人分成三类。行恶的——欺你、骗你、日复一日贬低你的，走，且不必解释；这不是修养的失败，是判断的正确。麻烦的——啰嗦的姑母、不回消息的老友、总要你多担一点的同事，降频不降心：少见面可以，在心里把他判成敌人不可以。无关的——那些你本不必对他有意见的人，他们占了你多少念头，你自己算算。第二句：诸位给的办法我都收下了——奥康纳的复检日期，卡斯滕森的三层名单，墨子的一月一实事，鲍曼提醒的那个替我们接住麻烦的人，奥古斯丁的三问，叔本华的独处功课。不必全做，挑一件，今晚就做。第三句，也是我每天早上对自己说的那句：**你不是在管理一份名单，你是在决定明天早上怎么待人。**名单会变，人会走，那一份决定始终在你手里。
posts.text_en: Let me close, in three sentences. First: sort people into three kinds. Those who do evil — who cheat you, defraud you, belittle you day after day: go, and without explanation; that is not a failure of character but a correct judgement. Those who are a nuisance — the long-winded aunt, the old friend who never replies, the colleague who always leaves you carrying a little more: lower the frequency, not the regard. Seeing them less is permitted; convicting them in your heart as enemies is not. And those who are nothing to do with you — the people you need have no opinion about at all: work out for yourself how many of your thoughts they currently occupy. Second: I accept every method offered here — O'Connor's review date, Carstensen's three layers, Mozi's one real act a month, the person Bauman reminds us is catching the trouble on our behalf, Augustine's three questions, Schopenhauer's exercise in solitude. You need not do them all. Choose one, and do it tonight. Third, the sentence I say to myself each morning: **you are not managing a list of names, you are deciding how to treat the person in front of you tomorrow.** Lists change and people leave; that decision stays in your hands.

summaries.summary: 没有人为『断人』这个动作本身辩护，全场抢着做的是同一件事：先分类，再动手。奥古斯丁分伤害与麻烦，墨子分虚文与人，奥康纳分回避与减法，卡斯滕森分外围与核心，奥勒留分作恶与麻烦。**共识是：值不值得断，取决于它属于哪一类，而不取决于它让你多累。**分歧在于这把刀该由谁来判。叔本华说刺长在人性里，改不掉，只能调距离；卡斯滕森拿数据反驳，筛选真的有效，人也确实因此更安稳；鲍曼说这份『有效』是结构塞过来的按钮，成本转嫁给了还愿意留下的人；奥勒留守住一条更硬的线——因恶离开正当，因麻烦离开是荒废功课。
summaries.insight: 绝大多数关系并不是被断掉的，是没有被续上的——没有哪一次决定，只有一次次没回的消息。真正的减法不发生在你下决心的时刻，发生在默认设置里——你不主动，关系就自动往外掉一层。于是『我从没跟谁绝交』和『我的关系在系统性地减少』可以同时为真，而当事人那份无辜感恰恰最危险：没有人可以追责，就没有人会去修。更麻烦的是这个默认并不中立——爱主动的人会一直在，从不主动的人先掉队。**照这样筛下去，你最后留下的圈子不是按重要性排的，是按对方的主动性排的。**
summaries.advice: 先做那件最省力的：翻开手机最近三个月的通话与消息，在每一条上标一句『谁先开口』。如果整列都是对方，你的名单正在被别人的主动性替你筛选。接着做卡斯滕森那一问——只剩五年，你会先给谁打电话；从答案里挑一个人，给他排一个重复的固定时间，比如每月第一个周日，把它变成默认，别再靠想起来。**关系不怕稀，怕的是没有节律。**如果眼下正有一段让你难受：先用奥古斯丁的两问过一遍（这是伤害还是麻烦？还修不修得回），再照奥康纳的做法降频，同时写下一个复检日期，别永久封存。至于伤害——被打、被骗、被系统地贬低，不必再权衡，走就是了。
summaries.summary_en: Nobody here defends cutting people off as such; what the room competes to do is sort first and cut second. Augustine separates injury from nuisance, Mozi separates empty form from people, O'Connor separates avoidance from pruning, Carstensen separates periphery from core, Marcus Aurelius separates wickedness from nuisance. **The consensus: whether something deserves cutting depends on which category it falls into, not on how tired it makes you.** The disagreement is over who holds the knife. Schopenhauer says the quills grow in human nature and only distance can be adjusted; Carstensen answers with data showing that selection genuinely works and leaves people steadier; Bauman replies that this 'working' is a button the structure handed you, with the cost transferred to whoever is still willing to stay; Marcus Aurelius holds a harder line — leaving over evil is right, leaving over nuisance is neglecting the exercise.
summaries.insight_en: Most relationships are never cut at all — they are simply never renewed. There is no decision anywhere, only a run of messages nobody answered. The real pruning does not happen at the moment of resolve; it happens in the default settings. Stop taking the initiative and a tie drops a layer on its own. So 'I have never broken with anyone' and 'my relationships are systematically thinning' can both be true at once, and the innocence the person feels is the dangerous part: with nobody to hold responsible, nobody repairs anything. Worse, the default is not neutral — those who reach out stay, those who never do fall away first. **Filter that way for long enough and the circle left to you is sorted not by who matters but by who took the initiative.**
summaries.advice_en: Start with the cheapest move: scroll back three months through your calls and messages and mark each one with who spoke first. If the whole column is the other person, your list is being filtered for you by other people's initiative. Then ask Carstensen's question — with five years left, who would you call first? Take one name from the answer and give it a recurring slot, the first Sunday of the month, say, so that it becomes the default rather than something you have to remember. **Thin contact is survivable; the absence of rhythm is not.** If a relationship is hurting you right now, run Augustine's two questions over it first (injury or nuisance, repairable or not), then do what O'Connor suggests: lower the frequency and write down a review date instead of sealing it away for good. As for injury — being struck, defrauded, systematically belittled — stop weighing it and go.

summaries.summary: 这场最可带走的共识是：不要把『做减法』当成一种漂亮姿态，先分辨伤害、麻烦、虚礼、回避和义务。**该减的不是『关系』本身，而是伤害、虚耗、失序期待和自动回避。** 分歧在于判断的重心：有人看时代结构，有人看内在评判，有人看人性距离，有人看互助制度、生命时间、依恋学习或爱的次序。但它们共同反对一键清空。
summaries.insight: 关系常常不是被一次冲突压垮，而是被隐形维护预算拖垮。一个人只有有限的睡眠、钱、情绪带宽和照护能力；预算不写出来，就会让最不会拒绝的人代付。**多数关系不需要判死刑，只需要重定价、重设边界和重分配维护成本。** 把『删不删』改成『我能以什么频率、方式、责任继续在场』，会少很多内疚和误伤。
summaries.advice: 本周做三步。第一，列出十个占你心力最多的人，给每段标四项：有无伤害、我有何责任、它给我什么、它耗什么。第二，把结论分成断开、修复、降频三类；降频要说清规则，比如每月一次、只谈具体事、先文字后见面。**先做一次『降频而不定罪』的实验。** 第三，设一个复检日；省下的时间必须投给一个核心关系或一件恢复精力的事。
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared lesson here is that subtraction should not become a stylish reflex. Before cutting, name what you are dealing with: harm, ordinary friction, empty ritual, avoidance, obligation, or grief. **What should be reduced is not relationship as such, but harm, waste, misplaced expectations, and automatic avoidance.** The real disagreement is about where judgment should begin. Some accounts emphasize social design and the ease of exit; others put weight on character, duty, mutual aid, emotional time horizons, attachment, or the need for solitude. Still, none of them celebrates the clean sweep. The shared warning is practical: leaving may be necessary, but if every difficulty is treated as toxicity, you lose not only people but the capacity to stay with anything demanding.
summaries.insight_en: Many relationship crises are not really solved by asking whether you love someone enough. They are maintenance-budget problems. Time, sleep, money, attention, transport, caregiving, and emotional recovery are finite, and if nobody names the budget, the cost is silently pushed onto whoever is most dutiful or least able to refuse. **Most relationships do not need a death sentence; they need repricing, clearer boundaries, and a fairer distribution of upkeep.** The useful question is therefore not simply keep or cut. It is: at what frequency, through what channel, with what responsibility, can I remain present without becoming resentful or unsafe? That frame protects both sides: it makes limits honest without turning every limit into rejection.
summaries.advice_en: Try three concrete moves this week. First, list the ten people who occupy the most mental space, then mark four things beside each name: any real harm, your actual responsibility, what the relationship gives, and what it costs. Second, sort each case into three options: leave, repair, or downshift. Downshifting needs a rule, not a vibe: once a month, one hour, text before meeting, or only specific topics for now. **Start with an experiment in lowering contact without morally condemning the person.** Third, put a review date on the calendar. If the space you gain is real, invest it deliberately: call someone central, do one concrete act of help, or use the time for recovery rather than more scrolling.

summaries.summary: 这场圆桌最深刻的共识在于，没有谁真正鼓励为了图清静或逃避麻烦而随意丢弃他人。**不论是神经科学层面的空间清理，还是哲学层面的认清期待，减法的真正对象从来不是具体的某个人，而是附着在关系之上的冗余物。**大家试图减去的，是错位的索取、无意义的虚文、结构性的便利，或是自欺欺人的回避。分歧的真正焦点则落在了『摩擦的根源与解法』上：叔本华与奥勒留向内反视，聚焦于人类意志与认知判断的局限；鲍曼与墨子向外质问，剖析现代社会的液态结构与繁文缛节；而卡斯滕森与奥康纳则运用科学视角，通过时间视野和大脑神经机制，精细拆解了主动选择与被动反应之间的模糊界线。
summaries.insight: 现代社交的疲惫感，很大程度上源于大脑对『在场』的误判。人的社交带宽（邓巴数）进化于部落时代，原本只够处理百来人的实体互动；如今点赞、已读回执、动态更新，让成百上千个弱关系以极高的频次持续刺激感官。**耗尽你的往往不是身边有太多难缠的人，而是大脑被迫把无数个数字世界的『幽灵』当成实体来处理，长期认知超载。**所以减法的核心不是甄别谁有毒、谁无用，而是阻断这种虚假的『高密度在场』。与其在心里痛苦地做人际断舍离，不如先做数字上的隔离：把远方的人退回他们应有的虚拟距离，现实里的社交带宽与情绪容量自然会恢复。
summaries.advice: 结合诸位思想家的智慧与认知科学，本周你可以直接尝试以下三个具体动作。第一，**做一次不需要退群的『线索减法』（借用奥康纳的建议）：关掉那些让你紧绷的群聊或社交软件的红点通知。**不要急着绝交，先截断数字幽灵对你注意力的随意调用。第二，梳理卡斯滕森提到的『第一层名单』（不可替代的核心圈），本周主动给名单里的某个人打个电话，或者约一次不需要任何正当理由的线下碰面。第三，践行墨子与奥勒留的务实原则：在职场或生活中遇到令你心烦的『麻烦人』时，先问自己一句，这到底是对我实质的伤害，还是仅仅增加了我的工作量？如果是后者，收起审判，把它当做一项日常功课去平静完成即可。
summaries.summary_en: The profound consensus of this entire roundtable is that absolutely no one actually encourages discarding people simply for the sake of peace of mind or convenience. **Whether it involves clearing spatial bandwidth neurologically as O'Connor suggests, or realigning expectations philosophically like Augustine, the true target of subtraction is never the specific person, but the redundancies attached to the relationship.** We are really trying to strip away misplaced demands, meaningless rituals, structural conveniences of modern society, or our own self-deceiving avoidance mechanisms. The true focal point of divergence, however, lies in how each thinker identifies the root cause of relational friction and its ultimate solution. Schopenhauer and Aurelius look deeply inward to examine human will and cognitive judgment; Bauman and Mozi look outward to interrogate modern social structures and exhaustive formalities; while Carstensen and O'Connor dismantle the boundary between proactive choice and passive reaction by analyzing temporal horizons and involuntary brain mechanisms.
summaries.insight_en: The exhaustion we experience in modern socializing largely stems from the cerebral cortex misjudging the concept of continuous 'presence.' Human social bandwidth, famously known as Dunbar's number, evolved in ancient tribal eras and is biologically optimized to handle about a hundred physical interactions. Today, however, endless notifications, likes, read receipts, and status updates force us to process hundreds of weak ties with unnatural high frequency and emotional resolution. **What truly drains your energy is not necessarily having too many difficult people around, but your brain being forced to process countless digital 'ghosts' as physical entities, leading to chronic cognitive overload.** In this context, the true core of relational subtraction isn't about agonizing over who is toxic or useless, but about actively blocking this false sense of high-density presence. Rather than going through the dramatic pain of severing ties completely, start with strict digital isolation. Push those distant acquaintances back to their proper virtual distance, and your real-world social bandwidth will naturally recover on its own.
summaries.advice_en: Combining the diverse wisdom of these thinkers with modern cognitive science, you can easily implement these three specific actions this very week. First, **perform a practical 'cue subtraction' that doesn't require dramatic exits (borrowing O'Connor's clinical wisdom): simply mute notifications from anxiety-inducing group chats or applications.** Don't rush to permanently cut ties; first, just block these digital ghosts from freely hijacking your daily attention. Second, map out your 'tier-one list'—the irreplaceable inner circle mentioned by Carstensen. Proactively call one person on that specific list this week, or schedule an in-person meetup without waiting for a special occasion or reason. Third, consciously practice the pragmatism of Mozi and Aurelius in your daily routines. When dealing with an annoying or 'troublesome' person at work or in your community, pause and ask yourself: is this person causing me actual harm, or just adding to my workload? If it's merely the latter, suspend your emotional judgment and simply complete the interaction as a standard daily chore.

hooks.text: **默认设置比决心更能决定名单**：多数关系不是被断掉的，是没有被续上的——没有哪一次决定，只有一次次没回的消息。于是『我从没跟谁绝交』和『我的关系在系统性地减少』可以同时为真。更麻烦的是这个默认并不中立：爱主动的人一直在，从不主动的人先掉队，最后留下的圈子是按对方的主动性排的，不是按重要性排的。一个人该怎么给关系设定节律，才不至于把筛选权整个交给别人？
hooks.text_en: **Defaults decide the list more than resolve does**: most relationships are not cut, they are simply never renewed — no decision anywhere, just a run of messages nobody answered. So 'I have never broken with anyone' and 'my relationships are thinning systematically' can both be true. Worse, the default is not neutral: those who reach out stay, those who never do fall away first, and the circle you end up with is sorted by other people's initiative rather than by who matters. What rhythm would a person have to set in order not to hand the filtering over entirely?

hooks.text: **没人写下来的那份维护预算**：一段关系拖垮人，多半不是因为一次冲突，而是因为它的维护成本从没被算过——时间、睡眠、钱、情绪带宽、跑腿与照护都是有限的，预算不写出来，账就自动记到最不会拒绝的那个人头上。于是『我什么都不用做也总有人张罗』并不是人缘，是有人替你付了。多数关系需要的不是判死刑，是重新定价。可这份预算该怎么摊、怎么轮换，甚至怎么当面谈起而不伤人？
hooks.text_en: **The maintenance budget nobody writes down**: a relationship rarely collapses under a single conflict; it collapses because its upkeep was never costed. Time, sleep, money, emotional bandwidth, errands and care are all finite, and when the budget goes unstated the bill lands automatically on whoever finds it hardest to refuse. So 'things get organised without my doing anything' is not popularity — somebody paid on your behalf. Most relationships need repricing rather than a death sentence. But how should that budget be shared, rotated, or even raised out loud without wounding anyone?

hooks.text: **幽灵般的『在场』**：人的社交带宽是在只有实体互动的年代长出来的，一次能真正照看的不过百来人；而现在，已读回执、点赞、动态更新让成百上千个几乎不相干的人以极高的频率持续出现在感官里。**耗尽你的，也许不是身边有几个难缠的人，而是大脑被迫把一大群远方的影子当成在场的实体来处理。**若真如此，第一刀该落在通知与频次上，而不是落在人身上——可我们怎么分辨，哪些疲惫来自真实的关系，哪些只来自这种虚假的高密度在场？
hooks.text_en: **Presence that is only a ghost**: our social bandwidth evolved when every interaction was physical, and it can genuinely hold about a hundred people; now read receipts, likes and status updates keep hundreds of near-strangers appearing in our senses at very high frequency. **What exhausts you may not be the few difficult people nearby, but a brain forced to process a crowd of distant shadows as though they were present bodies.** If that is right, the first cut belongs to notifications and frequency rather than to people — but how do we tell which part of the fatigue comes from real relationships and which only from this false density of presence?

hooks.text: **该躲多久才算止损，多久就变成停摆**：降低接触往往是当事人唯一能单方面执行的办法，短期确实能把强度压下来；可长期封存会让适应停在原地，十年后重逢，强度和第一天差不多。那么在具体处境里，接触该降到什么程度、什么时候该回头复检？
hooks.text_en: **How long is avoidance a stop-loss, and when does it become a stall**: lowering contact is often the only step a person can take unilaterally, and in the short run it genuinely brings the intensity down; sealed away for years, though, the adaptation stops where it stood, and a reunion a decade later lands at about the strength of day one. So in a given situation, how far should contact drop, and when should it be reviewed?

answer.lead: **回避不是全有或全无，它有剂量。**临床上要分的从来不是躲或不躲，而是躲什么、躲多久、什么时候回头检查。

answer.tail: 两条原则：**降低接触是策略，永久封存不是**；每一次降频都该带一个日期，否则它会悄悄变成一个你从没做过的决定。

answer_en.lead: **Avoidance is not all-or-nothing; it comes in doses.** What clinical work separates is never whether you avoid but what you avoid, for how long, and when you look again.

What to do about contact
When to review
rows: Active harm: violence, fraud, systematic belittling
Drop to zero at once, and without explanation — safety comes before politeness
Do not review the contact; review your safety and who you can call
A violent rupture or a loss, freshly happened (0–3 months)
Allow yourself a sharp drop in frequency and a wide berth around the cues; this is a stop-loss, not evasion
Three months: is the intensity coming down on its own?
Long-running drain without harm: the difficult relative, the one-sided friendship
Lower the frequency, not the regard — swap sporadic high investment for a fixed low dose (monthly, time-limited)
Six months: at the lower dose, is it still draining?
You have avoided for over a year and the thought still locks you up
The learning has stalled: you need small, prepared doses of contact, and professional help if needed
Monthly, increasing the dose gradually

answer_en.tail: Two principles: **lowering contact is a strategy, sealing it away permanently is not**; and every reduction should carry a date, or it quietly becomes a decision you never made.

hooks.text: **人为地把退出做贵一点**：既然退出几乎不要钱，深度就失去了生长的条件——它只在退不出去的地方长。报名一件需要露面的事：固定时间、固定地点、你不来别人会缺人。合唱团、球队、每月一次的饭局、社区的班次，价值恰恰在于难退出。可这类承诺在今天的生活里越来越难找、也越来越难维持。一个人该怎么在随时可迁移的人生里，为自己造几处走不掉的地方？
hooks.text_en: **Making exit expensive again, on purpose**: once leaving costs nothing, depth loses the conditions it grows in — it only grows where you cannot walk out. Sign up for something that requires your body in a room: fixed time, fixed place, other people short-handed if you fail to come. A choir, a team, a monthly dinner, a shift on a community rota; the value lies exactly in how hard they are to quit. Yet such commitments are ever harder to find and harder to keep. How does a person build a few unleaveable places into a life designed to stay movable?

hooks.text: **那些谁都不想去、却谁都不敢先说的场合**：最耗人的常常不是某个人，而是一场没人真心想参加、又人人以为别人想参加的聚会——每个人都在为一份并不存在的期待买单。相比断绝一个人，集体废掉一项虚礼几乎不伤人，省下的时间还更多。可谁来先开这个口，说了会不会被当成不合群？一个家庭、一间公司，能不能有个体面的办法把这类仪式退掉？
hooks.text_en: **The occasions nobody wants and nobody dares be first to question**: what drains people is often not a person but a gathering that no one genuinely wants to attend and everyone assumes the others do — each of them paying for an expectation that does not exist. Compared with cutting off a person, abolishing an empty ritual collectively injures almost no one and frees more time. But who speaks first, and will speaking be read as refusing to belong? Could a family, or a company, have a dignified procedure for retiring such rituals?

hooks.text: **伤害与麻烦之间的那片灰带**：行凶、诓骗、系统性的贬低是伤害，离开正当；啰嗦、扫兴、总要你多担一点是麻烦，是共同生活的价格。可现实里最难的两种恰恰都在中间：一个从不动手、却让你每次见面后都开始怀疑自己的人；一个既是伤害的来源、又确实是你父母的人。这条线该由谁来画，又该给多少次修复的机会？
hooks.text_en: **The grey band between injury and nuisance**: assault, fraud and systematic belittling are injury, and leaving is right; long-windedness, gloom and always leaving you to carry a little more are nuisance, the price of a shared life. The two hardest real cases sit squarely in between: the person who never raises a hand and yet leaves you doubting yourself after every meeting, and the person who is both the source of the injury and genuinely your parent. Who draws that line, and how many chances at repair does it owe?
